A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, and their text, equations, figures and appendices support comparison. The original appendices A–F largely correspond to Sections 7–12 in v2; Section 13 is new.

before.justification: v1 reports original Monte Carlo simulations of Berry–Esseen errors and Gaussian trajectory approximations in Section 4 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains those simulations and adds sensitivity analyses, synthetic attack-detection experiments and MNIST label-flipping experiments in Sections 12–13.

M1.justification: The local SGD and Aggr-GA/Client-GA constructions are retained. Algorithm 2 adds a specific sequential decision rule to the existing CUSUM/bootstrap framework: a bootstrap quantile plus c√n threshold, stopping at a threshold crossing, and an argmax estimate of attack onset.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates Gaussian approximations using the synthetic FRand-eff model. v2 adds attack-onset detection under client parameter shifts and a new MNIST classification setting with label-flipping attacks, substantially extending the evaluated data and task coverage.

E2.justification: The original comparison retains Aggr-GA, Client-GA and the functional-CLT/Brownian approximation. The new approximation ablations use the same comparator set, and the attack experiments introduce no competing detection methods.

E3.justification: New protocols include maximum relative quantile error, synthetic attack experiments with 500 iterations and 500 bootstrap samples, and a five-client MNIST experiment with three PCA components and 200 iterations. Section 12.7 inconsistently specifies synchronization values as 5, 50, 100 in prose but 5, 10, 15 in its table. Figure 3's caption changes N=1000 to N=500, matching the experimental text already present in both versions; this does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: Sections 12.3–12.5 add direct heterogeneity, synchronization and connection-matrix sensitivity tables, extending v1's narrower parameter investigations. Section 12.7 adds two explicit ablations testing how synchronization and heterogeneity affect the three trajectory approximations' quantile errors.

E5.justification: Tables 4–5 introduce intervals labeled 95% CI for estimated attack onset and stopping time; their construction is unspecified. The original simulations' repetition counts are retained, so the revision does not establish increased repetition of those experiments.

E6.justification: The original four figures retain identical plot images. New tables add sensitivity, quantile-error and attack-detection results: Table 4 reports a 0.046 false-positive rate and 0.966 detection probability at attack shift 1; Table 5 reports 0.06 under no attack and 0.90 under MNIST label flipping. These are newly reported outcomes, not improvements over corresponding v1 attack results.

T1.justification: Corollaries 12.1–12.2 introduce explicit moment, heterogeneity, synchronization and spectral-gap dependence, including allowance for tau≤theta*n; their detailed proofs are omitted. Equation 3.3 adds a sequential false-alarm argument. Existing proofs also receive mathematical corrections, including centering in Equation 8.2 and the telescoping sign in v1 Equation C.1 versus v2 Equation 9.1.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the main claims: Berry–Esseen bounds, two time-uniform Gaussian approximations, computation–communication trade-offs and bootstrap applications to attack detection. The added experiments support an application already claimed in v1 rather than redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit computational-cost and parallelization discussion for Aggr-GA versus Client-GA, interpretations of synchronization and topology dependence, and practical suggestions for synchronization-only monitoring and threshold tuning. The existing privacy, covariance-estimation and convexity qualifications are largely retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds substantial specifications for the new experiments, including connection-matrix construction, PCA preprocessing, the 40-parameter MNIST classifier, exact label swaps, bootstrap counts and warm-start estimation of the Hessian and covariance. The code hyperlink also changes GitHub owner from chebyshevtech to sohamb01. Threshold tuning and confidence-interval construction remain insufficiently specified.

R1.justification: Section 3.1 adds Mapakshi et al. (2025), Qian et al. (2024, ByMI) and Wang et al. (2020, Attack of the tails), positioning attack-onset detection relative to robustness and malicious-client identification. The broader related-work discussion remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section ordering are retained. Changes include local clarifications, expanded Section 3.1 and computational discussion, author affiliations, acknowledgments and numbered appendices. Section 3.1 also introduces redundant repetitions of the attack setup and CUSUM motivation.

P2.justification: The document receives different typography, title/author arrangement, running headers and text spacing throughout. v2 adds Algorithm 2, five numbered tables and two unnumbered ablation tables. The four original plot displays are retained and reflowed, with Figure 3's iteration-count caption corrected.

improvement.justification: The added sensitivity evidence, explicit synchronization dependence and synthetic/MNIST attack experiments make the practical implications more assessable than v1's largely motivational attack discussion. However, Algorithm 2 draws N(0,V_K) innovations while retaining K^(-1/2) scaling, unlike Theorem 3.1's N(0,K*V_K), leaving its calibration unclear. Together with conflicting ablation settings and unspecified interval construction, this limits the overall quality gain despite the useful additions.
